# ClaudeMC v1.19.7 — AutoMine: side strips & safety (Minecraft 1.21.1)

A focused release rewriting AutoMine's tunnel geometry and adding hazard
avoidance. AutoMine previously only ever dug a straight 2×1 tunnel; it now digs
proper side work and protects the player from falls, lava and water.

## Side strips that actually happen

AutoMine has a new **Layout** setting:

- **Pokehole** (default) — the xisuma-style branch-mine-with-pokeholes. Digs a
  2×1 main tunnel and, every `PokeEvery` blocks (default 4), digs a 1×1 hole
  out to the **left and right** (`PokeDepth` blocks deep, default 2). This
  reveals the maximum number of ore faces for the blocks mined and is what the
  user reported as missing.
- **Branch** — antennae layout: long perpendicular branches every
  `BranchEvery` blocks (default 11, i.e. a ~6-block solid gap between branches,
  the spacing shown to maximise ore-discovery efficiency) of `BranchLen`
  length (default 32, a stone-pickaxe's worth).
- **Tunnel** — straight 2×1 only, no side work.

The old `blocksForward % interval == 0` branch trigger (which could oscillate
on the spot) is replaced with `blocksForward - lastBranchAt >= interval`, and a
matching `lastPokeAt` tracker drives the poke-holes.

## Safety (new `Safety` and `Bridge` toggles, both on by default)

- **Fall protection** — before stepping forward, AutoMine checks the floor
  ahead. If there's a drop of more than 2 blocks it will either bridge the gap
  (place a block from the hotbar, if `Bridge` is on) or turn the tunnel 90° to
  walk away from the edge — so it no longer walks off ledges to its death.
- **Lava & water avoidance** — fluids are never mined into (mining a fluid
  block just drains it onto you). When lava or water is detected directly
  ahead, above, or beside a poke-hole, AutoMine seals the opening with a placed
  block or turns away instead of breaching it.
- **Damage response** — if the player starts taking damage while next to a
  fluid, AutoMine immediately walls off every adjacent fluid block from the
  hotbar to stem the flow before resuming.

Block placement picks a safe full block from the hotbar (skipping gravity
blocks like sand/gravel) and restores the previously selected slot afterwards.

All of AutoMine's existing behaviour — ore scanning with a configurable miss
chance, staff-evasion breaks, vein "surprise" look-arounds, random pauses and
the optional AI mining hint — is carried forward unchanged.
